reviews.review_title: Review at Le Comptoir de Tunis
reviews.review_text:
Steinthor
Iceland265 contributions
0
Perfect
Mar 2018 • Solo
I found this place by accident and oh my God, what a find. I stayed in Tunis for one night to start my trip around the country and consulted TripAdvisor, this was the closest restaurant with a good rating close to my hotel. Or so I thought. Never trust Google maps again. 

Anyway, I asked a policeman for directions after brushing off a couple of guys wanting to take advantage of the new foreigner in town. He ended up asking me for a few dinars as he was so badly paid. Never mind, he was nice and helpful. 

Once at the restaurant, miles away from Google maps destination, I was welcomed by a doorman who arranged a table for me. From then on, the evening turned perfect; I was seated upstairs, surrounded by several couples dining with a view over main bar area.

I had octopus carpaccio for starter, ever so beautifully arranged and tasty. Confit of duck was to die for, literally. If I was choosing my last meal, this would be my choice. The variety of flavours so great and all worked together, chocolate and cherry baked apples, beetroot puree. I didn't quite understand the menu but these are the flavours I got. Tiramisu at the end was really nice, not the usual Italian stuff but so good. 

It gives the impression of a very hip place, dj on site and loud music. Strangely it feels so appropriate and judging by the numbers of local people they like it. At the end of the evening all the chefs join guests.

I will end my trip around Tunisia in Tunis city and I'm going straight back to Le Comptoir for my final meal.

phenomenal food
Nov 2017 • Solo
i have eaten here three times this week. different dishes - starters, mains and deserts - the same line-up every single time. that makes nine different dishes tasted - for us engineers :) all nine dishes were perfect, and contained works of art like octopus carpaccio, seabass ceviche, anglerfish in pastis sauce, magret de canard, moelleux au chocolat, etc. as a solo patron out here, i paid about 40€ meal - invariably including a half-bottle of wine, water and coffee. service - very profesional. to me, the 5-star cuisine and the reasonable pricing makes this the best price/quality place i have ever eaten in. for people that like refined superior food - this is one of the places to visit in tunis! bon appetit!
